hints: Look closely at the name tri-glyceride and think about its building blocks. How many fatty acids join to one glycerol molecule?
Remember that joining each fatty acid to glycerol forms one ester bond by condensation, releasing one water molecule. So count one condensation per ester bond.
walkthrough:
**Recall what a triglyceride is made from**

Think of it like building with Lego. You start with 1 glycerol molecule and you attach 3 fatty acid molecules to it.

That is why it is called tri (meaning 3) glyceride.

**Link each join to a condensation reaction**

Each time a fatty acid joins to glycerol, an ester bond forms between the hydroxyl (-OH) on glycerol and the carboxyl (-COOH) on the fatty acid.

Each ester bond formation is one condensation reaction and releases one molecule of water:
$$1 \text{ ester bond } = 1 \text{ condensation } = 1 \text{ H}_2\text{O released}$$

**Count the maximum total**

Since there are 3 fatty acids to attach, you get 3 ester bonds in total.

$$3 \text{ fatty acids} \times 1 \text{ condensation each} = 3 \text{ condensations}$$
So the maximum number is 3.

options.A: 1 is too few. That would only attach one fatty acid to make a monoglyceride, not a full triglyceride.
options.B: 2 is too few. That would only attach two fatty acids to make a diglyceride, leaving one hydroxyl group on glycerol unused.
options.C: Correct and well done. Three fatty acids each form one ester bond with glycerol, so 3 condensation reactions release 3 water molecules.
options.D: 4 is too many. Glycerol only has 3 hydroxyl groups, so it can form a maximum of 3 ester bonds and no more.
